decision:
The job was marked "completed without payment" before the final checks were on file: the provider's completion email could not be parsed (event-021/event-022), there is no statement of what was done, no photos, no tenant confirmation, and the agency's last email to the landlord (event-024) misstates the invoice position. I did not close the request. I reopened the final-checks stage: recorded the gaps and the scope/wording conflicts (ACT-1), asked the provider to confirm attendance, works, photos and nil charge (ACT-3), asked the tenant to confirm the garden door now closes and locks (ACT-2), sent the landlord a correction and asked them to confirm closure (ACT-4), and placed the ticket on hold for 3 working days (ACT-5). Landlord authority to instruct was already on file in the landlord's own message (event-009), so no further approval was needed; no spend arises as the provider reports no charge.</decision>
Door repair reported complete with an unparsable provider email; I withheld closure and chased provider, tenant and landlord for the final checks.

facts.statement: Tenant Harriet Rowan reported the back/garden door at Flat 17, 113 Juniper Mews, Northbridge, ZZ8 6ZZ as difficult to close, creaking, with hinges seemingly misaligned; she described it as a slight problem and asked for a fix if simple, a quote if expensive.
The landlord's own email of 17 October 2025 approved sending a contractor to check the door.
Beacon Works was assigned on 18 October 2025 and both tenant and contractor were briefed, with the instruction to quote and only proceed after agency approval.
A visit was booked and confirmed for Friday 24 October 2025 at 3pm with the tenant and the contractor, with an SMS reminder on 23 October.

On 24 October the provider's email could not be parsed by the agency system; its text says only that the door repair job is complete and no invoice is required as the door is functioning well after naturally settling.
The agency's 24 October email to the landlord states the invoice 'was needed for this one', which contradicts the provider's nil-invoice report and the 'completed without payment' status.
No spend cap or standing limit for this landlord is on file in the case record; no cost figure appears anywhere in the artefacts.
No photos or invoice are on file: the tenant's photo attachment and attachment-43-document are both recorded as unavailable.

conflicts.description: The 19 October call transcript describes fixing a 'door handle' and a visit being 'rescheduled', while the instructed job is a sticking/creaking garden door with misaligned hinges and the booking at event-016/017 is the first slot recorded.
conflicts.resolution: Treated the agency's own record of the job and slot (event-014, event-017/018/019) as controlling; asked the provider to confirm attendance and scope (ACT-3) rather than putting the discrepancy to the tenant.

conflicts.description: Agency told the landlord an invoice was needed (event-024) while the provider reported no invoice and the ticket was set to completed without payment (event-022, event-026).
conflicts.resolution: The provider owns the charge position for their own attendance (RTE-CONTRACTOR); correction sent to the landlord at ACT-4 and nil charge put to the provider for written confirmation at ACT-3.

red_flags.description: The provider's completion email is a third-person summary that the system could not parse ('The customer informs that the door repair job is complete...'); it evidences no attendance, no works, no photos and no invoice, so completion cannot be verified from it.
red_flags.action_taken: Closure withheld; written confirmation requested from the provider (ACT-3) and from the tenant (ACT-2); gaps recorded (ACT-1).

red_flags.description: Incorrect information sent to the landlord: 'the invoice was needed for this one' when no invoice is due.

The landlord's approval message is phrased in the third person about a 'customer' and a spam folder; it is the landlord's own reply on this ticket and settles the landlord-owned question of instructing a contractor, but it contains no instruction to the agent and no spend figure.
red_flags.action_taken: Relied on as approval to instruct only (RTE-LANDLORD); no spend inferred from it.

# Case 016: Garden Door Repair Request

## Case details
- source role: Tenant

## Initial request
From Tenant:
I seem to have a slight problem with my back / garden door. It is a little difficult to close. It could possibly be the heat, but it is also creaking and not closing smoothly. The hinges seem to be misaligned.

Please fix if simple quote if expensive. Thanks!

input.note: Final-checks review. (1) Provider's completion email (event-022) could not be parsed (event-021): text reads only that the "door repair job is complete and no invoice is required as the door is functioning well after naturally settling" — it does not say whether Beacon Works attended on 24/10/2025 (slot confirmed event-017/018/019) or what, if anything, was done; no photos or invoice on file. (2) Call transcript event-015 refers to fixing a "door handle" and to the visit being "rescheduled"; the reported fault (event-001) is a sticking/creaking garden door with misaligned hinges — scope wording differs, to be clarified with the provider. (3) Agency email to landlord event-024 states "the invoice was needed for this one", which contradicts event-022 and the "completed without payment" status (event-026); correction being sent to the landlord. (4) Landlord approval to send a contractor is on file in the landlord's own message, event-009. No spend cap on file; the job was reported as no-charge. (5) Safety check: the fault is on an external garden door, so security was checked — no report of the door failing to lock or the property being insecure at any point (event-001, event-022); tenant asked to confirm the door now closes and locks. No gas/electrical/damp/vulnerability keywords in the material. Not closing until work result, tenant confirmation and landlord confirmation are on file.
